stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
Indicates the model is categorized under text-generation pipelines.
Tags confirm its relevance to transformers, safetensors, and the Llama family of models.

stories.title: RoboTTT: Context Scaling for Robot Policies
stories.author: Linxi "Jim" Fan
bullet_points: Introduces RoboTTT, a new framework for robot policies that scales visuomotor context to 8K timesteps.
Achieves this massive context scaling without increasing inference latency, a significant technical hurdle overcome.
Enables advanced capabilities such as one-shot in-context imitation and on-the-fly policy improvement in robotics.

stories.title: RoboTTT: Context Scaling for Robot Policies
stories.author: Linxi "Jim" Fan
bullet_points: Introduces RoboTTT, a novel framework for robot policies that significantly scales visuomotor context up to 8K timesteps.
Achieves this massive context scaling without increasing inference latency, a major technical hurdle overcome.
Enables new capabilities such as one-shot in-context imitation from video and on-the-fly policy improvement.

stories.title: First atmosphere found on Earth-like planet in habitable zone of distant star
stories.author: neversaydie
bullet_points: Detection of the first atmosphere on an Earth-like exoplanet.
The planet is located within the habitable zone of its distant star.
This represents a major step forward in exoplanetary science and astrobiology.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on the Hugging Face platform.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized under text-generation, indicating its primary function as a large language model.
Key associated technologies include transformers and safetensors, standard components in modern NLP/ML workflows.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the 'deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro' model on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized for text generation tasks, indicating its capability in language modeling.
It is associated with key ML technologies like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance shows up to 90% speed increase when benchmarked using Aider.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using its MLX engine.
The performance improvements result in faster response times and higher quality model outputs.
The updated engine also demonstrates reduced memory consumption when running models.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, offering an open-source framework for building personal AI agents.
A key feature is its local-first design, allowing AI to run entirely on the user's own hardware.
It integrates native support for Ollama, facilitating the use of local LLMs.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for performance optimization.
This integration specifically targets Apple Silicon hardware, enhancing local AI capabilities on Macs.
The feature is currently available in preview, signaling an ongoing push for optimized on-device AI.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed to integrate with messaging applications.
It utilizes local AI coding agents, emphasizing on-device processing for privacy and control.
The core value proposition is connecting communication platforms to local, private AI capabilities.

stories.title: TikTok is testing an AI likeness detection tool
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: TikTok is piloting an opt-in AI likeness detection tool for creators.
The tool allows users to report content featuring unauthorized AI likenesses.
This development mirrors similar efforts being undertaken by competitors like YouTube.

stories.title: Google-backed satellites for wildfire detection launch as smoke chokes US, Canada
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: Google-backed FireSat program utilizes advanced satellite technology for wildfire detection.
The system is designed to identify wildfires that current satellite monitoring methods overlook.
The launch is timely, addressing severe wildfire smoke issues across the US and Canada.

stories.title: San Francisco orders Apple, Google to remove nudify apps from app stores
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: San Francisco has mandated that Apple and Google remove 'nudify' applications from their respective app stores.
The regulatory action targets apps designed to influence user behavior, suggesting a growing focus on digital ethics and manipulative design.
The enforcement action implies potential revenue loss for Google and Apple, who are estimated to have earned millions from these apps.

stories.title: Pretraining Data Can Be Poisoned through Computational Propaganda
stories.author: Kyle Lo
bullet_points: The research demonstrates that Large Language Models (LLMs) can be poisoned during pretraining using computational propaganda.
This poisoning can introduce harmful behaviors into LLMs that are challenging to detect and mitigate.
The attack is feasible beyond previous, limited studies that focused only on established, small-scale data sources.

stories.title: SceneBind: Binding What and Where Across Vision, Audio and Language
stories.author: Eli Shlizerman
bullet_points: SceneBind introduces an omni-modal representation capable of integrating vision, audio, and language for scene understanding.
It specifically addresses a limitation in existing encoders by providing explicit 3D spatial structure, moving beyond just instance-level semantics.
The core innovation involves representing scenes as semantic-spatial entities using a combination of global and object-centric embeddings.

stories.title: AutoSynthesis: An agentic system for automated meta-analysis
stories.author: Stefan Feuerriegel
bullet_points: Introduces AutoSynthesis, an end-to-end multi-agent system designed for automated meta-analysis.
Addresses the current bottleneck of manual and difficult-to-scale quantitative evidence synthesis in research.
The system takes a natural language research question and autonomously handles literature search, screening, and data extraction.

stories.title: When Words Are Safe But Actions Kill: Probing Physical Danger Beyond Text Safety in Hidden-State Risk Space
stories.author: Ke Xu
bullet_points: Investigates the critical gap between text-level safety and physical safety when LLMs control embodied agents.
Demonstrates that linguistically safe instructions can lead to dangerous physical outcomes when grounded in the real world.
Uses hidden-state analysis to show that 'content danger' and 'physical danger' are separable signals within LLM representations.

stories.title: Pretraining Data Can Be Poisoned through Computational Propaganda
stories.author: Kyle Lo
bullet_points: The research demonstrates that Large Language Models (LLMs) can be poisoned during pretraining using computational propaganda.
Existing poisoning research is limited because it focuses on small, established datasets (like Wikipedia) and ignores large-scale, heterogeneous corpora.
The study highlights the difficulty in detecting and mitigating harmful behaviors introduced by poisoned pretraining data, especially when interacting with data curation pipelines.

stories.title: LG monitors silently install software through Windows Update without consent
stories.author: baranul
bullet_points: LG is reportedly installing software on Windows systems via Windows Update.
The installation occurs silently and without explicit user consent.
This raises significant concerns regarding user privacy and software control.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 introduces significant performance improvements.
Enhanced GGUF model compatibility is now available via llama.cpp integration.
The update broadens model support across various hardware, augmenting the MLX engine on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra.
The model is specifically designed for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is optimized for supporting long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for subagents within Claude Code.
The new feature set includes the capability for web search functionality in Claude Code.
This enhancement expands the capabilities of local LLM orchestration via Ollama.

stories.title: Apple’s plot to crush OpenAI
stories.author: David Pierce
bullet_points: Apple has initiated a lawsuit against OpenAI.
The lawsuit contains intense allegations, though experts suggest some practices may be standard industry procedure.
The article aims to analyze Apple's motivations for engaging in a public legal dispute with OpenAI.

stories.title: SciDiagramEdit: Learning to Edit Scientific Diagrams from Paper Revisions
stories.author: Jürgen Schmidhuber
bullet_points: SciDiagramEdit addresses the manual and time-consuming process of editing scientific figures during paper revisions.
The system aims to automate figure editing using natural language instructions.
The challenge lies in the complex visual grammar of scientific diagrams, which combine diverse elements like plots, schematics, and arrows.

stories.title: Beyond Success Rate: Cost-Aware Evaluation of Offensive and Defensive Security Agents
stories.author: Yaron Singer
bullet_points: The research proposes a new evaluation metric for AI security agents that incorporates operational cost alongside success rate.
Traditional evaluations often ignore the resource consumption (inference budget) of security agents during complex tasks.
The study tests this cost-aware evaluation on offensive (Cybench) and defensive (Splunk BOTS v1) security scenarios.

stories.title: SearchOS-V1: Towards Robust Open-Domain Information-Seeking Agent Collaboration
stories.author: Zhicheng Dou
bullet_points: Introduces SearchOS, a system-level multi-agent framework designed to improve information-seeking capabilities.
Addresses a critical limitation in current LLM agents: struggling to track task progress and avoid repetitive loops during complex web searches.
Focuses on enhancing the robustness and efficiency of agents when initial search attempts fail to provide useful evidence.

stories.title: teLLMe Why (Ain't Nothing but a Jam): Exploratory Causal Analysis of Urban Driving Data
stories.author: Jorge Ortiz
bullet_points: Introduces 'teLLMe,' a system designed for exploratory causal analysis of urban driving datasets.
Addresses the challenge of answering causal questions (e.g., 'How would rain change traffic density?') using purely observational traffic data.
Combines causal structure learning with structured event tables derived from dashcam annotations to facilitate analysis.

stories.title: In-Place Tokenizer Expansion for Pre-trained LLMs
stories.author: Mathias Lechner
bullet_points: Current LLM tokenizers are fixed based on initial pre-training corpus priorities.
Adding new languages later can lead to inefficient tokenization, increasing latency and resource usage.
The issue is exacerbated in compact models where embedding matrices are a larger fraction of total parameters compared to large cloud models.

stories.title: Online Neural Space Time Memory for Dynamic Novel View Synthesis
stories.author: Xuan Luo
bullet_points: Addresses the real-time constraint challenge in novel view synthesis from streaming videos.
Identifies the trade-off between maintaining long-horizon memory and computational efficiency.
Proposes a solution to overcome the high computational cost of gradient-based memory updates in dynamic scenes.

stories.title: Mutable Low-Rank Sketches for Retrain-Free Recommendation
stories.author: Nick Clayton
bullet_points: Addresses the 'embedding staleness' bottleneck in two-stage recommendation systems.
Introduces 'mutable sketches' using a KP-tree to store user preferences sparsely.
Allows for on-the-fly embedding recomputation upon new user ratings, improving timeliness.

stories.title: In-Place Tokenizer Expansion for Pre-trained LLMs
stories.author: Mathias Lechner
bullet_points: Current LLM tokenizers are fixed based on initial pre-training corpus priorities.
Adding new languages later often results in inefficient tokenization (more tokens per word), increasing latency and resource use.
The issue is exacerbated in compact models where embedding matrix size is a greater constraint compared to large cloud models.

stories.title: NeuronSoup: Evolving Asynchronous, Shared-Neuron Temporal Graphs without Backpropagation
stories.author: Subodh Kalia
bullet_points: Introduces NeuronSoup, a novel neural computation architecture moving away from traditional synchronous, layer-by-layer processing.
Features asynchronous, delay-mediated signal propagation using a pool of physically shared neurons.
Aims to operate without relying on the standard backpropagation algorithm for learning.

stories.title: BadWAM: When World-Action Models Dream Right but Act Wrong
stories.author: Xinchao Wang
bullet_points: World-Action Models (WAMs) are a new paradigm for embodied control, linking action generation with future world prediction.
The paper introduces 'BadWAM' to challenge the assumption that this coupling inherently leads to robust and safe robot behavior.
BadWAM provides a unified framework for modeling and evaluating the failures in these advanced control models.

stories.title: SciDiagramEdit: Learning to Edit Scientific Diagrams from Paper Revisions
stories.author: Jürgen Schmidhuber
bullet_points: SciDiagramEdit addresses the manual and time-consuming process of editing scientific figures during manuscript revisions.
The system aims to automate figure editing using natural language instructions.
The challenge lies in the complex, heterogeneous visual grammar of scientific diagrams (schematics, plots, arrows, etc.).

stories.title: Bridge Evidence: Static Retrieval Utility Does Not Predict Causal Utility in Multi-Step Agentic Search
stories.author: Shubham Chatterjee
bullet_points: Traditional retrieval evaluation (static usefulness) fails when language models act as multi-step search agents.
The utility of a retrieved document in agentic search depends on its potential to enable future actions, not just answering the current query.
The research highlights a critical gap between static document relevance and dynamic, multi-turn reasoning capabilities in AI agents.

stories.title: Beyond the Leaderboard: Design Lessons for Trustworthy Multimodal VQA
stories.author: Steven A. Hicks
bullet_points: The research focuses on designing trustworthy and interpretable multimodal AI for healthcare, specifically Visual Question Answering (VQA).
The study retrospectively analyzes nine systems using GI endoscopy data to evaluate question answering and explanation quality.
While parameter-efficient adaptation improves performance, it doesn't guarantee faithful or complete clinical reasoning in AI models.

stories.title: TikStance: A Multimodal and Hierarchical Dataset for Multi-target Stance Analysis in TikTok Political Conversations
stories.author: Bowen Zhang
bullet_points: Introduces TikStance, a new multimodal and hierarchical dataset specifically for stance analysis in political conversations on TikTok.
Addresses the current limitation in computational analysis due to the scarcity of datasets that combine audiovisual data with conversational context from short-video platforms.
The dataset is designed around the 2024 U.S. election cycle, covering discussions related to three major political figures.

stories.title: In-Place Tokenizer Expansion for Pre-trained LLMs
stories.author: Mathias Lechner
bullet_points: Current LLM tokenizers are fixed based on initial pre-training corpus priorities.
Adding new languages later can lead to inefficient tokenization (more tokens per word), increasing latency and resource use.
The issue is exacerbated in compact models where embedding matrix size is a greater constraint compared to large cloud models.

stories.title: Expanding the Lexicon of Ge'ez Based African Languages: A Comparative Study of Amharic and Tigrinya
stories.author: Wolfgang Nejdl
bullet_points: Addresses the performance degradation of Multilingual Pre-trained Language Models (PLMs) on low-resource, non-Latin-script African languages.
Introduces VEXMLM, a vocabulary-extended variant of XLM-R specifically designed to improve performance on Amharic and Tigrinya.
Evaluates the model across 19 African languages, highlighting the challenge of high Out-of-Vocabulary (OOV) rates in current NLP models.

stories.title: Mask-Aware Policy Gradients for Diffusion Language Models
stories.author: Philipp Krähenbühl
bullet_points: The research addresses the challenge of applying Reinforcement Learning (RL) to Masked Diffusion Language Models (MDLMs).
A key difficulty in current methods is the intractability of log-likelihood estimation in MDLMs.
The proposed work introduces 'Mask-Aware Policy Gradients' to account for the sequential decision-making process during MDLM generation.

stories.title: NextBSD project revived: Apple's FOSS user-space tools on the FreeBSD kernel
stories.author: nextbsd.org via lproven
bullet_points: The NextBSD project has been revived, focusing on integrating Apple's FOSS user-space tools.
This effort aims to bring specific open-source utilities from Apple into the FreeBSD kernel environment.
The news is relevant to the open-source community and operating system development, particularly for FreeBSD users.

stories.title: Porting a 128-expert MoE (Gemma-4 26B-A4B) to AWS Inferentia2 — where every rank weighted the wrong experts
stories.author: xbill
bullet_points: The article details the complex process of porting a large Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model (Gemma-4 26B-A4B) to AWS Inferentia2 hardware.
The porting effort encountered significant technical hurdles, including a dual-path FFN and a sparse expert loop that failed to trace correctly.
A critical bug was identified where the device output was empty despite successful CPU reference and passing unit tests.

stories.title: My Inferentia port matched its reference token-for-token — and still output garbage
stories.author: xbill
bullet_points: The article details a complex engineering challenge in porting a large language model (Gemma-4 31B) to AWS Inferentia2 hardware.
The standard tensor-parallel recipe used for smaller models failed at the 31B scale, requiring a specialized NxD ModelBuilder solution.
A critical issue is highlighted where successful validation metrics do not guarantee correct output quality ('passing validation lies to your face').

stories.title: Can a Semantic Cache Become Your Primary Retrieval Layer?
stories.author: surajrkhonde
bullet_points: The article explores the concept of implementing a semantic cache layer.
This cache is proposed to sit in front of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems.
The author suggests this semantic caching approach could be a significant, yet overlooked, cost-saving measure.
